calculation: categorical (no-excuse / excuse-required / all-mail) + list of excuses
copy_geo_coverage: states + Puerto Rico + U.S. Virgin Islands (per NCSL table)
definition: Whether an excuse is required for absentee/mail voting, and which categories qualify (noting Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands appear in NCSL table).
geo_coverage: states + Puerto Rico + U.S. Virgin Islands (per NCSL table)
how_to_read: 1 = yes (excuse required); 0 = no.
payoff_hook: Mail voting rules at a glance: do you need a qualifying reason to vote by mail?
suggested_cta: If mail voting is restricted, look at early in-person options.
watch_out_for: Excuse categories vary—don’t guess; check official guidance for your state.
why_it_matters: Whether an excuse is required for absentee/mail voting, and which categories qualify (noting Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands appear in NCSL table).

definition: Average margin of victory across major statewide races (President, Governor, U.S. Senate, etc.) in the most recent cycle.
display_name: Average margin in top statewide races
how_to_read: Lower margin means outcomes tend to be tighter.
payoff_hook: Average margin of victory in big statewide races—smaller margins = more competitive.
suggested_cta: Competitive states benefit from consistent participation.
ui_title: Average margin in top statewide races
watch_out_for: Don’t overpromise ‘your vote decides’; use ‘your vote is part of the margin.’
why_it_matters: Average margin of victory across major statewide races (President, Governor, U.S. Senate, etc.) in the most recent cycle.

definition: Average time voters report waiting to vote (survey-based) or administrative estimates where available.
how_to_read: Lower is better for convenience; compare to national average.
payoff_hook: The line factor: how long voters typically wait in your state.
suggested_cta: Vote early/off-peak if your area has longer waits.
watch_out_for: Wait times vary hugely by county and time of day—use as a planning cue.
why_it_matters: Average time voters report waiting to vote (survey-based) or administrative estimates where available.

definition: Count of statewide ballot measures/referenda in the next election date (varies by state).
display_name: Number of ballot measures on upcoming ballot
how_to_read: More measures means more direct issue decisions by voters.
payoff_hook: Direct democracy meter: how many statewide ballot measures you’ll vote on next.
recommended_viz: Count badge + list of measures with summaries.
suggested_cta: Preview the measures and decide where you stand.
ui_title: Number of ballot measures on upcoming ballot
watch_out_for: Counts change as measures qualify; keep it updated.
why_it_matters: Count of statewide ballot measures/referenda in the next election date (varies by state).

copy_primary_sources: https://electionlab.mit.edu/data (for results datasets) ; official state election results
definition: How often statewide races in this state are decided by small margins (e.g., ≤1% or ≤10,000 votes) over last N cycles.
how_to_read: Higher means more frequent close margins.
payoff_hook: How often statewide races are close—where a small turnout shift can decide outcomes.
primary_sources: https://electionlab.mit.edu/data (for results datasets) ; official state election results
suggested_cta: If races are often close, your vote has extra leverage.
watch_out_for: Use multi-cycle averages; single elections can be outliers.
why_it_matters: How often statewide races in this state are decided by small margins (e.g., ≤1% or ≤10,000 votes) over last N cycles.

definition: Share of voters expressing confidence their vote was counted as intended (SPAE).
how_to_read: Higher is better for confidence and legitimacy.
payoff_hook: Trust metric: the share of voters who feel confident their ballot was counted as intended.
suggested_cta: Learn how your ballot is processed and tracked.
watch_out_for: Use neutral framing; pair with ‘how votes are counted’ explainer.
why_it_matters: Share of voters expressing confidence their vote was counted as intended (SPAE).

definition: Whether the jurisdiction has voting representation in the U.S. House/Senate or is represented by a non-voting delegate/resident commissioner.
how_to_read: Show the representation type and what it can/can’t do.
payoff_hook: Territories: how representation in Congress works (voting member vs nonvoting delegate/resident commissioner).
suggested_cta: Point to local elections and advocacy pathways.
watch_out_for: Keep terminology accurate and up to date.
why_it_matters: Whether the jurisdiction has voting representation in the U.S. House/Senate or is represented by a non-voting delegate/resident commissioner.

copy_update_frequency: biennial (EAVS; drop box questions added in recent cycles)
definition: Density of ballot drop boxes for returning mail ballots (where permitted and tracked).
display_name: Ballot drop boxes per 100,000 registered voters
how_to_read: Higher can mean easier, more flexible returns for mail ballots.
payoff_hook: Drop box access: how many ballot drop boxes are available relative to population.
recommended_viz: Map + count per 100k; quick ‘closest drop box’ CTA.
suggested_cta: If using a drop box, return well before the deadline.
ui_title: Ballot drop boxes per 100,000 registered voters
update_frequency: biennial (EAVS; drop box questions added in recent cycles)
watch_out_for: Locations/hours matter; pair with a map of nearby drop boxes.
why_it_matters: Density of ballot drop boxes for returning mail ballots (where permitted and tracked).

calculation: count of calendar days of early in-person voting window (state-level policy; may vary by county)
definition: Number of days of early in-person voting available for a general election (consumer-facing: 'How many days you can vote early').
how_to_read: More days generally means more flexibility for busy schedules.
payoff_hook: Your voting window: how many calendar days early in-person voting is available.
suggested_cta: Pick a specific early-vote day as your default plan.
watch_out_for: Some locations may not be open every day—use it as a planning guide, not exact hours.
why_it_matters: Number of days of early in-person voting available for a general election (consumer-facing: 'How many days you can vote early').

definition: Overall index comparing election administration performance across states (composite of multiple indicators).
display_name: Election Performance Index (EPI) overall score / rank
how_to_read: Higher score/rank suggests stronger performance across multiple indicators.
payoff_hook: A nonpartisan ‘election administration scoreboard’ comparing how states run elections.
suggested_cta: Explore what your state does well—and what’s improving.
ui_title: Election Performance Index (EPI) overall score / rank
watch_out_for: Composite indices can hide tradeoffs—let users drill into sub-metrics (waits, rejections, etc.).
why_it_matters: Overall index comparing election administration performance across states (composite of multiple indicators).

definition: Whether residents can vote for U.S. President in the general election (states + DC yes; territories no, with exceptions for eligible voters who reside in states).
display_name: Can residents vote for U.S. President in general election?
how_to_read: Yes/No. (Territories generally cannot in the general election.)
payoff_hook: Territories: whether residents can vote for President in the general election.
suggested_cta: Highlight the elections where residents *do* have direct votes.
ui_title: Can residents vote for U.S. President in general election?
watch_out_for: Explain primaries vs general election clearly.
why_it_matters: Whether residents can vote for U.S. President in the general election (states + DC yes; territories no, with exceptions for eligible voters who reside in states).

definition: Percent of returned mail/absentee ballots rejected (signature issues, lateness, etc., depending on state definitions).
how_to_read: Lower is better. A small percent can still mean many ballots in big states.
payoff_hook: Mail voting reliability: how often mail ballots get rejected in your state.
suggested_cta: Return early, follow signature instructions, and track your ballot.
watch_out_for: Rejections can be avoidable (late return, signature issues). Encourage tracking and early return.
why_it_matters: Percent of returned mail/absentee ballots rejected (signature issues, lateness, etc., depending on state definitions).

definition: Metrics on ballots sent/returned/accepted for uniformed services and overseas voters (UOCAVA-related).
how_to_read: Higher is better; it reflects the end-to-end process from sending to counting.
payoff_hook: For military & overseas voters: what share of transmitted UOCAVA ballots are counted.
suggested_cta: If you’re overseas/military, start early and track your ballot.
watch_out_for: Some losses are due to non-return; emphasize sending early and tracking.
why_it_matters: Metrics on ballots sent/returned/accepted for uniformed services and overseas voters (UOCAVA-related).

definition: Share of voters who cast ballots early in-person (including in-person absentee where applicable).
how_to_read: Higher means more people vote before Election Day at early sites.
payoff_hook: How your state votes: the share of ballots cast early in person.
recommended_viz: Stacked bar + calendar view for early window.
suggested_cta: Pick a day/time in the early window to avoid lines.
watch_out_for: Early voting periods and site coverage vary within states.
why_it_matters: Share of voters who cast ballots early in-person (including in-person absentee where applicable).

definition: Share of voters who cast ballots in-person on Election Day.
display_name: Voting mode share – Election Day in-person
how_to_read: Higher means Election Day dominates; lower means more early/mail voting.
payoff_hook: How your state votes: the share of ballots cast on Election Day in person.
recommended_viz: Stacked bar (Election Day vs early vs mail).
suggested_cta: Choose the mode that fits your schedule.
ui_title: Voting mode share – Election Day in-person
watch_out_for: Availability and culture differ; don’t treat a ‘low’ share as bad—just different.
why_it_matters: Share of voters who cast ballots in-person on Election Day.

definition: Share of voters who cast ballots by mail/absentee.
how_to_read: Higher means mail voting is a major pathway.
payoff_hook: How your state votes: the share of ballots cast by mail/absentee.
suggested_cta: If voting by mail, track your ballot and return it early.
watch_out_for: If mail is common, emphasize deadlines and signature rules to avoid rejection.
why_it_matters: Share of voters who cast ballots by mail/absentee.

definition: Whether any voter can request an absentee/mail ballot without an excuse.
how_to_read: 1 = yes (no excuse needed); 0 = an excuse is required.
payoff_hook: Mail voting rules at a glance: can any voter request a mail/absentee ballot without a special reason?
suggested_cta: If you might be busy on Election Day, consider mail voting (and return early).
watch_out_for: Even in no-excuse states, deadlines and ID/signature rules can matter.
why_it_matters: Whether any voter can request an absentee/mail ballot without an excuse.

definition: Whether online voter registration is available (EPI includes as an indicator in some versions).
how_to_read: 1 = yes; 0 = no.
payoff_hook: Convenience boost: can you register (or update) online instead of on paper?
suggested_cta: Check your registration status today.
watch_out_for: Online systems can have cutoffs—don’t wait until the deadline.
why_it_matters: Whether online voter registration is available (EPI includes as an indicator in some versions).

copy_geo_coverage: US; potentially state breakdowns depending on survey sample
definition: Percent of voters who waited more than 30 minutes in line (often more meaningful than average).
geo_coverage: US; potentially state breakdowns depending on survey sample
how_to_read: Lower is better; track improvements over cycles.
payoff_hook: A ‘hassle risk’ metric: what share of voters wait more than 30 minutes.
suggested_cta: If the risk is high, plan early voting or mail (if available).
watch_out_for: Hotspots are local—pair with county-level info when possible.
why_it_matters: Percent of voters who waited more than 30 minutes in line (often more meaningful than average).

calculation: P(state pivotal in Electoral College) * P(state vote tied | pivotal scenario)
copy_update_frequency: per election forecast (daily in campaign season)
definition: Modeled probability that one vote in a given state is decisive in the presidential election (requires an election forecast; concept popularized by Gelman/Silver/Edlin).
how_to_read: Best used as an explainer, not a precise promise.
payoff_hook: A modeled ‘pivotality’ estimate: how likely a single vote is to be decisive in the presidential race.
suggested_cta: Even when not pivotal, voting shapes down-ballot outcomes.
update_frequency: per election forecast (daily in campaign season)
watch_out_for: Model-based and sensitive to assumptions; present as ‘relative’ rather than absolute.
why_it_matters: Modeled probability that one vote in a given state is decisive in the presidential election (requires an election forecast; concept popularized by Gelman/Silver/Edlin).

definition: Not a numeric score by default: a short explainer surfaced in-app describing evidence that participation relates to representation/responsiveness (with citations).
display_name: Evidence link: turnout & policy responsiveness (context metric)
how_to_read: Use as context—link to studies and plain-English takeaways.
payoff_hook: Evidence snapshot: how participation levels connect to political responsiveness in research.
suggested_cta: Voting is one lever—also contact reps and show up locally.
ui_title: Evidence link: turnout & policy responsiveness (context metric)
watch_out_for: Avoid claiming causality when studies are correlational; cite sources.
why_it_matters: Not a numeric score by default: a short explainer surfaced in-app describing evidence that participation relates to representation/responsiveness (with citations).

definition: Density of in-person voting locations relative to registered voters (proxy for convenience and potential congestion).
how_to_read: Higher = more polling places relative to registered voters (not a guarantee of shorter lines).
payoff_hook: A quick proxy for how ‘spread out’ polling places are: more places per voters can mean easier access.
recommended_viz: Rank + distribution plot; optional map shading.
suggested_cta: Check your polling place and consider early voting if access looks tight.
watch_out_for: Precinct size, staffing, and voting mode mix also affect lines.
why_it_matters: Density of in-person voting locations relative to registered voters (proxy for convenience and potential congestion).

definition: Difference between presidential-year turnout and midterm turnout (same denominator).
how_to_read: Bigger gaps mean many voters sit out midterms—your vote can matter more.
payoff_hook: The ‘drop‑off’: how much turnout falls in midterms compared with presidential years.
suggested_cta: If you vote in presidential years, make midterms your superpower.
watch_out_for: Use the same turnout measure (e.g., VEP) for both elections.
why_it_matters: Difference between presidential-year turnout and midterm turnout (same denominator).

definition: Percent of provisional ballots rejected.
how_to_read: Lower is better. High rates mean follow-up steps may be important.
payoff_hook: Provisional ballot follow-through: how often provisional ballots end up not counting.
suggested_cta: If you vote provisionally, follow your state’s cure steps promptly.
watch_out_for: Provisional rules differ; emphasize ‘how to cure’ and deadlines.
why_it_matters: Percent of provisional ballots rejected.

definition: Percent of citizen voting-age population who report being registered to vote (CPS).
how_to_read: Higher means more people can vote without last‑minute paperwork.
payoff_hook: The share of eligible citizens who are registered—your state’s ‘ready-to-vote’ rate.
recommended_viz: Gauge + rank; trend line over cycles.
suggested_cta: If you’re not registered (or unsure), check your status.
watch_out_for: Registration rules and list maintenance differ; compare trends over time too.
why_it_matters: Percent of citizen voting-age population who report being registered to vote (CPS).

definition: Share of voters reporting problems (registration, lines, mail ballot issues, etc.) in the voting process (SPAE).
how_to_read: Lower is better; highlight what the most common issues are.
payoff_hook: Problem rate: the share of voters who reported any voting issue (registration, ID, lines, etc.).
suggested_cta: Use the checklist to avoid common problems.
watch_out_for: Combine with ‘what to bring’ and ‘how to fix’ tips—avoid doom framing.
why_it_matters: Share of voters reporting problems (registration, lines, mail ballot issues, etc.) in the voting process (SPAE).

calculation: residual_votes / ballots_cast (contest-specific; EPI uses standardized approach)
definition: Rate of ballots with no valid vote recorded for a given contest (proxy for ballot design / equipment / voter information).
how_to_read: Lower can indicate clearer ballots and smoother tabulation.
payoff_hook: Ballot usability signal: how often ballots have an uncounted selection for a top race (lower is better).
suggested_cta: Review your ballot carefully and use recommended marking guidance.
watch_out_for: Only comparable within similar election types and ballot designs.
why_it_matters: Rate of ballots with no valid vote recorded for a given contest (proxy for ballot design / equipment / voter information).

calculation: votes_cast / registered (or VAP) depending on territory reporting
copy_primary_sources: https://www.electionguide.org/ (IFES ElectionGuide) ; territory election authority sites (e.g., https://vivote.gov/)
definition: Turnout in the most recent territory-wide general election (governor/legislature/delegate).
how_to_read: Higher means more local civic participation.
payoff_hook: Local turnout: how many eligible voters participated in the most recent territory-wide election.
primary_sources: https://www.electionguide.org/ (IFES ElectionGuide) ; territory election authority sites (e.g., https://vivote.gov/)
suggested_cta: Make local elections a habit—they often affect daily life most.
watch_out_for: Data availability varies—cite the election authority source.
why_it_matters: Turnout in the most recent territory-wide general election (governor/legislature/delegate).

definition: Percent of citizen voting-age population (CVAP) reporting they voted in the most recent federal election (CPS survey-based).
display_name: Turnout (Citizen Voting-Age Population) – last general election
how_to_read: Use for ‘people like me’ comparisons (age, race/ethnicity, education).
payoff_hook: A survey-based turnout estimate: who *says* they voted (citizens only). Great for demographic breakouts.
recommended_viz: Group comparisons + confidence band; small multiples by demographic.
suggested_cta: Find your peer group’s turnout and set a personal goal.
ui_title: Turnout (Citizen Voting-Age Population) – last general election
watch_out_for: Survey estimates differ from official-count-based turnout and have sampling error.
why_it_matters: Percent of citizen voting-age population (CVAP) reporting they voted in the most recent federal election (CPS survey-based).

definition: Difference in turnout between younger voters (e.g., 18–29) and older voters (e.g., 65+).
display_name: Turnout gap: young vs older voters
how_to_read: Bigger gaps mean policymaking may skew toward older voters.
payoff_hook: Participation gap by age: which age groups are underrepresented at the polls.
recommended_viz: Dumbbell chart (young vs older) + cohort callout.
suggested_cta: Bring a friend in your age group to vote together.
ui_title: Turnout gap: young vs older voters
watch_out_for: Avoid shaming; use empowering ‘join your age cohort’ messaging.
why_it_matters: Difference in turnout between younger voters (e.g., 18–29) and older voters (e.g., 65+).

definition: Difference in turnout between college graduates and non-graduates (CPS).
how_to_read: Bigger gaps can signal unequal representation.
payoff_hook: Participation gap by education: who votes less often—and how big the gap is.
suggested_cta: Make a plan that fits your schedule and logistics.
watch_out_for: Focus on barriers and solutions, not blame.
why_it_matters: Difference in turnout between college graduates and non-graduates (CPS).

definition: Difference in turnout between higher- and lower-income groups (CPS categories).
display_name: Turnout gap: higher vs lower income
how_to_read: Bigger gaps can mean lower-income needs are under-heard.
payoff_hook: Participation gap by income: how uneven turnout is across income levels.
suggested_cta: Use early/mail options to lower time costs (if available).
ui_title: Turnout gap: higher vs lower income
watch_out_for: Emphasize convenience options and practical help.
why_it_matters: Difference in turnout between higher- and lower-income groups (CPS categories).

definition: Differences in turnout by race/ethnicity categories (CPS).
how_to_read: Bigger gaps can mean unequal voice in outcomes.
payoff_hook: Participation gap by race/ethnicity: how evenly different communities are represented.
recommended_viz: Small multiples by group + gap highlight.
suggested_cta: Share resources within your community network.
watch_out_for: Use careful, respectful language; emphasize access and empowerment.
why_it_matters: Differences in turnout by race/ethnicity categories (CPS).

definition: Change in turnout vs the previous election of the same type (presidential-to-presidential or midterm-to-midterm).
display_name: Turnout momentum (change vs prior same-type election)
how_to_read: Positive = turnout increased; negative = turnout fell (percentage points).
payoff_hook: Momentum check: is turnout rising or slipping since the last election of the same type?
suggested_cta: Be the difference-maker: plan a low-friction voting method.
ui_title: Turnout momentum (change vs prior same-type election)
watch_out_for: Population changes and election competitiveness can move this year-to-year.
why_it_matters: Change in turnout vs the previous election of the same type (presidential-to-presidential or midterm-to-midterm).

copy_geo_coverage: US, states, DC (territories may be separate)
copy_update_frequency: after each general election (estimates may update through certification)
definition: Percent of the voting-eligible population (VEP) who cast a ballot in the most recent general election (presidential or midterm).
geo_coverage: US, states, DC (territories may be separate)
how_to_read: Compare to the national average and to nearby states; small shifts can be meaningful.
payoff_hook: How engaged is your state? This is the share of eligible voters who showed up last time.
recommended_viz: Rank + percentile badge; trend sparkline across cycles.
suggested_cta: See what’s on your ballot and make a plan (date/mode).
update_frequency: after each general election (estimates may update through certification)
watch_out_for: Compare presidential-to-presidential or midterm-to-midterm—turnout naturally differs by election type.
why_it_matters: Percent of the voting-eligible population (VEP) who cast a ballot in the most recent general election (presidential or midterm).

copy_geo_coverage: US; limited state-level depending on CPS tables
definition: Composite measure of turnout inequality across demographics (e.g., average absolute gap across age, education, income).
geo_coverage: US; limited state-level depending on CPS tables
how_to_read: Higher risk means bigger representation gaps.
payoff_hook: A risk flag when turnout gaps suggest some groups’ voices are missing.
suggested_cta: Share tools that lower barriers for underrepresented voters.
watch_out_for: Be transparent about how you compute it (inputs, weights).
why_it_matters: Composite measure of turnout inequality across demographics (e.g., average absolute gap across age, education, income).

copy_geo_coverage: US; possible state breakouts depending on sample
definition: Share of voters rating their voting experience positively (SPAE survey).
geo_coverage: US; possible state breakouts depending on sample
how_to_read: Higher suggests a smoother, less stressful experience.
payoff_hook: How voters felt about voting in your state—an overall experience rating.
recommended_viz: Smiley-scale + trend; compare to national average.
suggested_cta: Help improve elections: report issues and share feedback.
watch_out_for: Survey-based and may vary by community; invite users to share experiences too.
why_it_matters: Share of voters rating their voting experience positively (SPAE survey).
